type: u32 at +0x54 of the placement record: 4 = placed, 5 = stored template or initially inactive object (bit 0); in RAM the same word reads 1 = active with an actor, 2 = placed but without an actor yet, 5 = never instantiated by itself
structure: On every record of the placement class the file word is exactly 4 or 5: tutorial (class 104) 377 and 296, Mining (class 98) 381 and 236. Bit 0 set marks the objects a level stores for its scripts to clone or activate: the game-element libraries (`GameElement_*.lvl` layers: breakable-rock halves and quarters, track switches, the mine-train and elemental-gate templates, icons, enemy projectiles) and level-specific inactive actors (cutscene actors, triggers, a rescued miner). The `.lvl` layer is a related but distinct signal: 27 flagged records on Mining are in no library, 31 library members are placed with the bit clear (the Automaton's parts). In the running game every record of the class is constructed with the same class pointer 0x80481674; those stored with 4 read 1 and carry an actor pointer at +0xF4, those stored with 5 read 5 and carry no actor, their stored and current positions unchanged at the storage coordinates.
meaning: A record with bit 0 set is not placed at its coordinates: it is a resource the level's scripts clone (`clone||at|facing`) or activate elsewhere, and drawing it where the file stores it shows a mine train at the origin, a track switch outside the level, rock halves in empty space. The editor keeps those records in the hidden 'Templates and disabled objects' layer and in Project > Resources on every level, with the class detected for the file (scene-roles.mjs), and links a placed twin when one exists. Not a visibility property: nothing here is written to the file, and where a script later creates the object is not read. The RAM state 2 (placed, no actor) belongs to objects the game has not activated yet, such as the Automaton's parts before the boss breaks; it is reported, not interpreted. CONFIRMED would need the same reads repeated on a second boot and a second level; the tutorial's earlier comparison (level.tutorial.scripted-preview-poses) and this Mining read are the two concordant observations behind LIKELY.
